title: July Is Ice Cream Month! Scoop Up These Cool Facts
summary:
Did you know July is the yummiest month of the year? It’s National Ice Cream Month! Back in 1984, President Ronald Reagan decided ice cream deserved a whole month of celebration—and he even made the third Sunday of July National Ice Cream Day. So grab a cone and let’s dig into some frosty fun facts!

Ice cream has been around for a long, long time. The first frozen dessert like it was made in China during the Tang Dynasty, with milk, flour, and something called camphor. Later, Arab chefs in the 9th century created a version with milk and sugar. It didn’t reach America until 1744, when a governor served strawberry ice cream at a fancy dinner. Everyone loved it! George Washington once spent $200 on ice cream in one summer—that was a fortune back then. Thomas Jefferson even wrote his own vanilla ice cream recipe.

But for years, ice cream was only for rich people because ice was hard to store. That changed in 1851 when the first ice cream factory opened in Pennsylvania. Now, Americans gobble up about 23 pounds of ice cream per person every year! California makes the most, but the biggest fans live in Rhode Island, Wisconsin, and Washington, D.C.

Your favorite flavor might say something about you. A scientist found that vanilla lovers are adventurous risk-takers, chocolate fans are outgoing and energetic, strawberry fans are thoughtful and loyal, and mint chocolate chip lovers are ambitious and confident. Which one are you?

Ice cream can also be record-breaking. In 2014, a dairy in Wisconsin made the world’s largest scoop. They poured 733 tubs of ice cream into a giant freezer box, then five snow sculptors carved it into a scoop shape. It weighed 3,010 pounds and stood over five feet tall! After the record was confirmed, everyone at the festival got to eat it. And in 2023, a shop in Japan sold the most expensive ice cream ever: a single serving cost $6,696, with rare truffles, gold leaf, and fancy cheeses. That’s one pricey scoop!
why_it_matters: Ice cream connects you to people across the centuries - from ancient Chinese emperors to America's founders - all of whom enjoyed cold treats, reminding you that simple joys are timeless.

background_read: President Ronald Reagan (who served as U.S. president from 1981 to 1989) loved ice cream so much that he made the whole month of July a time to celebrate it.
Ice cream's journey began in ancient China and later spread to Arab countries, where it was made with milk and sugar, then to Europe and America through trade and colonization.
In the 1800s, ice was still a luxury, so only wealthy people could enjoy ice cream until factories started mass-producing it in the mid-19th century.
Article_Structure: WHO: President Ronald Reagan, and ice cream lovers across America.
WHAT: July is National Ice Cream Month with fun facts about ice cream's history, records, and favorite flavors.
WHERE: In the United States (with origins in China and the Middle East).
WHY: To celebrate a popular dessert and remember how it became a part of American life.

perspectives.description: Ice cream brings families and friends together, especially during summer, and celebrating it as a nation creates shared joy.
Some nutrition experts caution that eating too much ice cream, which is high in sugar and fat, can be unhealthy, and they encourage moderation.
Learning about ice cream's long history can spark curiosity about how other everyday foods traveled around the world.
